solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Courier car is carrying a lot of cheese

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the cheese word loses its tail
a vehicle carrying a load holds it inside, so the car word wraps round the cheese

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, a station wagon
feta, the Greek cheese, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A delivery van is loaded with most of a consignment of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Car alone suggests no particular model; an estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estafette is a military messenger on horseback who carries dispatches, i.e. a courier.

clue.text: Panic surrounding cat in minor fight

indicators.note: surrounding means one word encircles the other, holding the cat word inside

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
mog is British slang for a cat (short for moggy)

explanation.surface: Someone panics as a cat gets into a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARMOGE is Spenser's word for a skirmish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarmoge is an archaic Spenserian variant of skirmish, a small-scale clash.

clue.text: English composer, one behind bars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., Tudor composer of church music
second meaning: a tavern-keeper, who serves from behind a bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'One behind bars' suggests a prisoner, but the bars are the counters of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverner is both the surname of the Tudor musician John Taverner and an old word for an innkeeper or publican.

clue.text: Advertisement space connected with one Middle-Easterner

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement
an en is a printer's space, half an em
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An advert's blank space is linked to a man from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adeni is a native of Aden, the port city in Yemen, so a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Mock a Tesla that's stalled at high speed

indicators.note: something stalled is put into a stall, so these letters are enclosed by the mocking word

parts.note: to flout is to mock or scorn
taken as written
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Jeering at an electric car that has broken down while going fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but here it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out is an idiom for going as fast as possible, with full effort or speed.

clue.text: Tube journey not half taking long

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is dropped and the other kept
taking means taking in, so the shortened journey word holds the other inside

parts.note: the first half of travel, a journey
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An Underground trip that is only half as long as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube journey' reads as one trip on the London Underground, but Tube alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the air tube running from the larynx to the lungs.

clue.text: Only one large comprehensive in say, a London borough

indicators.note: keeping only one of a doubled large means the word sheds one of its two L's
in places the shortened word inside the abbreviation for say

parts.note: e.g., for example, i.e. say
all-in means comprehensive; one of its two large-letter L's goes

explanation.surface: A borough with a single big comprehensive school, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, but here the word means all-inclusive; L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough of west London, famous for its film studios.

clue.text: Trim Spaniards turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dons are Spanish gentlemen

explanation.surface: Neatly dressed Spaniards arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOD is a Scots adjective meaning neat or trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Snod is a Scots dialect word for neat or tidy, so trim as an adjective.

clue.text: Counsel out of focus in college

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so the central letter is taken out

parts.note: to teach is to counsel or instruct

explanation.surface: A blurry lawyer at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the five-letter TEACH is A, so losing its focus leaves the answer. Counsel looks like a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Tech is short for technical college, a further-education institution.

clue.text: Hairy task ordered for Hindu warrior

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A difficult job was demanded of a Hindu fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kshatriya are the second of the four Hindu varnas, the caste of rulers and warriors.

clue.text: A large amount of horse mackerel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., a great quantity (often plural)
second meaning: a fish of the jack family

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a big catch of one fish, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scad is informal for a large quantity and also the name of the horse mackerel, a carangid fish.

clue.text: Dullards working in laundries not independent

indicators.note: the abbreviation for independent must be dropped from the word before it is rearranged
working suggests letters being worked over into a new order

parts.note: laundries with I, for independent, removed

explanation.surface: Dim-witted staff are employed in launderettes that belong to a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurdane is an archaic word for a lazy, stupid person, so lurdanes are dullards or idlers.

clue.text: Crazy pass missing out both wings

definitions.note: An adjective defining a noun: fair in Mephisto because Chambers allows crazy as a noun for a craze, which is exactly what a rave is.

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters, and both are left off

parts.note: to pass along is to travel

explanation.surface: A wild pass in football that misses both wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings suggests wide players on a pitch; here they are the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a craze or passing enthusiasm, the sense of crazy as a noun for the latest fad.

clue.text: Absent girl seen by lake in Asian wood

parts.note: A is the register abbreviation for absent
gal is an informal word for girl
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A missing young woman is spotted near a lake in an Asian forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Agalloch is eaglewood or aloeswood, the fragrant resinous wood of an Asian tree.

clue.text: River of Italian city

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
o' is a short form of of

explanation.surface: Naming the river that flows through an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trento is the capital city of Trentino in northern Italy, site of the Council of Trent.

clue.text: Food stocking said to be for old Virginians

indicators.note: said means we go by how the words are pronounced, not how they are written

parts.note: tucker is Australian slang for food; non-rhotic speech drops the R
hose are stockings

explanation.surface: Provisions and hosiery are claimed to be meant for Virginians of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a British accent, tucker hose runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuckahoes was a nickname for the inhabitants of eastern, lowland Virginia, after a root eaten there.

clue.text: A dish put out for paragon

indicators.note: put out can mean disturbed or knocked out of place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish is served up for someone perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidha (siddha) is, in Hinduism, a perfected one who has attained spiritual powers, hence a paragon.

clue.text: Second World War commando back in large town not unknown

indicators.note: an unknown in algebra is a letter like x or y, and this one is to be dropped
in places the back word inside the shortened town word

parts.note: city without the Y
hind means back or rear

explanation.surface: A wartime commando returns to a big town where he is recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in' looks like a reversal instruction, but back is a word for rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were British special forces who fought behind Japanese lines in Burma in 1943-44.

clue.text: Bishop blessed in old case long forgotten

indicators.note: forgotten means left out, so the abbreviation for long is dropped from the fodder
blessed is a mild curse like blasted, implying the letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: the words without L, for long

explanation.surface: A bishop is consecrated inside an ancient chest that has long been forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese, as opposed to a suffragan or assistant.

clue.text: One society owning estates is isolated

parts.note: Roman numeral one
S is an abbreviation for society
landed gentry own estates

explanation.surface: A club for the landed gentry is cut off from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To island something is to set it apart like an island, so islanded means cut off or isolated.

clue.text: Help to bring about trick on leader

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Assisting a scheme to fool the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduce is to contribute or tend towards a result, i.e. to help bring it about.

clue.text: Car picked up close to a fiddle

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car
on can mean next to or close to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car was collected in an almost fraudulent deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to a' looks like an instruction to take the last letter of a, but close to means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cremona is a violin made at Cremona by the Amati, Guarneri or Stradivari, and fiddle is another word for violin.

clue.text: Moderate peacekeepers overlooking former Liberal party leader

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeepers
David Steel led the British Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988

explanation.surface: Moderate peacekeepers are watching an ex-Liberal leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, overlooking puts the first piece above the second. 'Moderate' reads as an adjective, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsteel is to remove the hardness from, soften or relent, so to moderate.

clue.text: Old dilapidated church, shortly before end of mass organ stops

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters of old rearranged
CE abbreviates the Church of England

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of mass

explanation.surface: A ruined old church's organ falls silent shortly before the end of the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is the name of a soft-toned organ stop, so dolces are organ stops.

clue.text: I rejected original fancy Hindu decorations

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so one I is removed from the fodder
fancy suggests something elaborate and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: original with one I removed

explanation.surface: Turning down unusual, elaborate Hindu ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoli are colourful floor patterns of powder or rice made at Hindu festivals such as Diwali.

clue.text: Foam on back of aircraft upfront

parts.note: aero- relates to aircraft

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket, the on side is the leg side

explanation.surface: Foam has been sprayed on the rear of the aeroplane, and on the front too.
explanation.walkthrough: Upfront places the aircraft piece first. The on side and leg side are the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogel is an ultralight solid in which the liquid of a gel is replaced by gas, a rigid foam.

clue.text: Male learner in confines of Calcutta?

definitions.text: Male learner in confines of Calcutta?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the boundary letters
the confines of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Calcutta
L for learner, as on L-plates
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A boy studying within Calcutta's limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a chela is a disciple in India, and Calcutta (Kolkata) is an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is a pupil or disciple of a guru in Hinduism, a learner on the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Shout in depression after losing wife

indicators.note: losing means a letter is lost, so the abbreviation for wife is dropped

parts.note: a hollow is a depression in the ground
W is the standard abbreviation for wife, the letter lost

explanation.surface: Crying out in despair after a wife's death.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression reads as low spirits, but it is a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollo is a variant of holler or halloo, a call or shout to attract attention.

clue.text: A certain rolling river in part of France

indicators.note: rolling suggests tumbling over, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: one can mean a certain, as in one Mr Smith
R abbreviates river

explanation.surface: A river rolls along through a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orne is itself a river, but here the definition is the department named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orne is a department of Normandy in north-west France, an administrative region of the country.

clue.text: Lewd desire of male chauvinist

indicators.note: of means taken out of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of male and start of chauvinist

explanation.surface: The lustful urges of a sexist man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lech, as a noun, is a lustful craving or lecherous desire, as well as the person who has it.

clue.text: Three articles written about introduction of Nigella, a goddess

indicators.note: written about means set down around, so the articles enclose the introduction
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the articles a, the and a
the first letter of Nigella

explanation.surface: Three pieces have been written on Nigella Lawson, a TV cookery goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson, the British TV cook, is often called a domestic goddess; only her initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Triumph over weedy stuff by Native American ending in waffle

parts.note: ore, or oreweed, is seaweed
the Crow are a Native American people of Montana

indicators.note: ending in means only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of waffle

explanation.surface: Victory over some weeds is followed by a Native American ending a long ramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Orecrowe is Spenser's spelling of overcrow, to crow over or triumph over someone.

clue.text: Charles Darwin's forensic test

indicators.note: the possessive marks the test as belonging to the name, held within its letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of Charles and start of Darwin

explanation.surface: A forensic examination devised by the great naturalist.
explanation.definitionFit: ESDA, electrostatic detection apparatus, is a forensic test revealing indented writing on paper.

clue.text: Expecting enclosure that's fortified

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ring of walls round a fortress or town

explanation.walkthrough: Expecting reads as anticipating a fortified enclosure; it is a separate meaning, pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Enceinte is both an adjective meaning pregnant and a noun for the defensive wall enclosing a fortified place.

clue.text: African encampment, authentic for retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: real means authentic

explanation.surface: A genuine African camp to withdraw to.
explanation.definitionFit: Laer is a variant of laager, the South African word for a camp defended by a circle of wagons.

clue.text: Marks right away covering gentle US terrain

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the abbreviation for right is removed
covering means wrapping round, so the shortened word encloses the other

parts.note: scars, marks, losing R for right
bland means mild or gentle

explanation.surface: Scars disappear, giving way to soft American landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Gentle looks like a description of the terrain, but it is the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Scablands are bare eroded basalt plains, notably the Channeled Scablands of Washington State in the US.
